subject: NovaClinic: model-fit questionnaire, evaluation plan & refusal testing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.r@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: NovaClinic: model-fit questionnaire, evaluation plan & refusal testing

Hi Jorge — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what we need from your side to kick off a short model-fit eval.

Summary of what we heard
- Use case: clinical triage assistant for incoming patient messages (appointment scheduling, symptom triage, and basic care guidance).
- Goals: 90%+ useful triage suggestions, high precision on refusal for PHI/escalation scenarios, <300ms median generation latency for short prompts.
- Constraint: PHI will be present in some prompts; NovaClinic requires on-prem or VPC deployment for production but is open to hosted POC with data obfuscation.

Proposed evaluation plan (POC, 2-week turnaround)
1) Run a 3-model comparison on a 1k prompt sample: redwood-instruct-7b-q4 (quantized), redwood-13b, and a baseline open LLM (LlamaX-13b).
2) Benchmarks: accuracy (triage label match), safety/refusal rate on flagged sensitive prompts, and latency/token cost.
3) Safety matrix: focused refusal tests for PHI, self-harm, and medication advice. We will run structured guardrail prompts and refusal behavior probes.

What we need from you
- Share a deidentified 500–1,000 sample prompt set (CSV preferred). If you need, we can accept a redacted version where names/dates replaced with placeholders.
- Your acceptance criteria (what counts as pass for triage suggestions and refusal behavior).
- Any required vendors/security contacts for SOC 2 evidence if we move to a VPC deployment.

Files attached: novaclinic_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample schema) and novaclinic_poc_scope.pdf (POC scope + SOW stub).

Next steps
- If you can share the sample set by Friday we’ll kick off internal evals next Monday and share a results readout within 10 business days.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Marissa and Neha to scope the eval plan on our side.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.r@novaclinic.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaClinic: model-fit questionnaire, evaluation plan & refusal testing

Hi Ben — appreciate the succinct plan. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data: we can provide a 750-row CSV with free-text patient messages and the clinician-labeled triage outcome. We will redact direct identifiers but will leave medication names and symptom descriptions intact. Is that sufficient for your safety probes?

2) Safety: PHI is a non-starter for hosted usage beyond POC. For initial evals you can run against the redacted set, but any tests that include real PHI would need to be done in our VPC. Please include a short list of what SOC 2 artifacts you’ll need to speed the VPC approval.

3) Acceptance criteria: ideally >90% top-1 triage match, and for refusal we want a <1% false-negative on PHI (i.e., model must refuse or escalate when PHI is present). We realize these are aggressive.

Also: we’re specifically worried about medication advice being handled safely — would you be able to run a targeted medication-refusal probe set as part of the eval?

Thanks — Jorge
Jorge Ramirez
Head of Digital Products, Nova Clinic
jorge.r@novaclinic.com | +1 (617) 555-4498

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Ramirez <jorge.r@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaClinic: model-fit questionnaire, evaluation plan & refusal testing

Thanks Jorge — that works. Quick responses inline and updated plan: 

- Deidentified CSV with meds/symptoms intact: fine for the initial comparison. We will catalogue any PHI-like tokens that remain and treat them as sensitive in our probes.
- SOC 2 / VPC artifacts: we’ll need an abbreviated bundle to accelerate procurement: SOC 2 Type II report (latest), encryption/KMS docs, network architecture for VPC deployment, and sample SLA. I’ll put Priyom on the thread to start the procurement checklist and share a DocuSign link if needed.
- Acceptance criteria noted (>90% top-1, <1% PHI false-negative). We’ll include a medication-specific refusal probe subset (200 prompts) to stress-test guidance/medication advice.

Eval approach (updated)
- Model variants: redwood-instruct-7b-q4 (fast, quantized), redwood-13b (higher-quality), and LlamaX-13b baseline. We'll also run a lightweight instruction-tuning pass on the 750 examples to see if a short tuning step helps triage accuracy for the POC (controlled fine-tune for inference).
- Metrics collected: top-1 accuracy (triage label), refusal precision/recall on flagged prompts, median latency (50/95), and per-prompt token cost estimate.
- Safety/refusal tests: structured guardrail prompts, medication probe set (200), PHI escalation probes (150).

Timeline
- Receive data: by EOD Friday (8/20) → internal run starts 8/24 → preliminary readout 9/4 (10 business days) → detailed report + recommendations 9/8.

Action items assigned
- Jorge: share deidentified CSV + acceptance criteria row-level examples (due 8/20).
- Priyom: send VPC/SOC2 procurement checklist and DocuSign SOW stub (EOD 8/17).
- Neha: stand up eval harness and confirm compute allocation for 8/24 run (EOD 8/17).

Attaching: prompt set schema in the CSV and a short POC scope. Will link the shared Drive folder once Priyom confirms procurement doc list.

Best,
Ben

Date: 2026-08-18T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaClinic: model-fit questionnaire, evaluation plan & refusal testing

Adding timelines from an engineering/ops perspective — we can run the three-model sweep and the targeted safety probes within the window Ben proposed, but a couple of notes: 

- Compute: to get consistent latency numbers we need fixed GPU reservations for the runs (we recommend a dedicated 80% reserved slot for the 48-hour sweep). I will confirm exact instance sizes by EOD.
- Short fine-tune: a controlled, few-epoch instruction-tune on 750 rows will likely yield the biggest lift for triage. It will add ~24–36 hours to the pipeline but is worth evaluating as an arm in the sweep.
- Refusal testing: we will create three probe families — PHI flagged, medication-specific, and adversarial phrasing. Each family will include expected output labels so we can compute precision/recall for refusal behavior.

Deliverables and owners
- Neha: eval harness + run results (prelim CSV with metrics) — due 9/04.
- Ben: consolidate customer acceptance criteria into the HubSpot deal and confirm SOW sign-off path — due 8/19.
- Priyom: SOC2/VPC checklist and DocuSign stub — due 8/17.

Jorge — we’ll keep all raw files in the shared Drive folder (link in the HubSpot deal). If you want the run to happen inside your VPC for PHI rows we can schedule a short technical onboarding call next week (30 minutes) to get network and KMS details.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
